# Shopware Storefront — route, controller and template map

How a URL becomes HTML. The controller loads a Page through its PageLoader and hands it to `renderStorefront()`, which resolves the template through the theme inheritance chain — so your own template at the same path wins over the core one.

**57 `renderStorefront()` calls across 18 controllers.**

## Contents

- [The chain](#the-chain)
- [Route to template](#route-to-template)
- [Templates by route](#templates-by-route)
- [Controllers without a route attribute](#controllers-without-a-route-attribute)

## The chain

```
HTTP request
  -> Route            #[Route(path, name, methods, defaults)]
  -> Controller       a method on a *Controller class
  -> PageLoader       builds the Page struct, dispatches PageLoadedEvent
  -> renderStorefront('@Storefront/storefront/...')
  -> Twig template    resolved through theme inheritance
```

To add data to an existing page, subscribe to its `*PageLoadedEvent` and call `addExtension()` — no controller override is needed. To change markup, override the template. Reach for a controller override only for genuinely new routes.

## Controllers without a route attribute

These render a template without an adjacent `#[Route]`. They are reached through exception handling, an ESI include or a parent route rather than directly by URL.

- `ErrorController::error` renders `storefront/page/content/index.html.twig`
- `ErrorController::error` renders `storefront/page/error/index.html.twig`
